title: Code of Hammurabi: Marriage, Dowry, and Inheritance Statutes
description: Old Babylonian legal statutes regulating marriage contracts, bridal gifts (tirhatu), dowry (sheriqtu), divorce, and concubinage in Mesopotamia.
primary_source: Code of Hammurabi §§128-176 (tr. L. W. King, 1915)

title: Sumerian Flood Story (Eridu Genesis)
description: Early Mesopotamian deluge and creation narrative preserved on Nippur tablet CBS 10673, attesting Near Eastern flood motifs.

title: Herodotus on Arabian Frankincense, Myrrh, and Spice Cultivation
description: Classical Greek ethnographic account of South Arabian aromatics, agricultural harvesting practices, and overland spice trade.

title: Strabo on Pre-Islamic Arabian Kinship and Caravan Polities
description: Greco-Roman geographic description of Nabataean and South Arabian social structures, marriage customs, and caravan commerce.

title: Mu'allaqah of Imru' al-Qays (Pre-Islamic Arabic Qasidah Tradition)
description: Canonical pre-Islamic Arabian ode exemplifying jahiliyyah poetic conventions, desert ecology, and oral performance culture.
primary_source: Al-Mu'allaqat, Imru' al-Qays (tr. F. E. Johnson, 1894, Internet Archive)

title: Plague of 'Amwas and Year of Ashes ('Am al-Ramadah)
description: Severe epidemic in Greater Syria paired with famine and drought in the Hijaz during 'Umar ibn al-Khattab's caliphate, prompting quarantine and grain-relief measures.

title: 'Abd al-Malik's Epigraphic Gold Dinar and Silver Dirham Reform
description: Replacement of Byzantine- and Sasanian-style coinage with standardized Arabic epigraphic currency and fiscal diwan Arabization.
primary_source: al-Baladhuri, Futuh al-Buldan (tr. P. K. Hitti, Internet Archive)

title: Abu Yusuf's Kitab al-Kharaj (Abbasid Land Tax & Fiscal Treatise)
description: Foundational Hanafi fiscal treatise commissioned by Harun al-Rashid addressing kharaj, 'ushr, jizya, sharecropping, and agrarian taxation tensions.
primary_source: Abu Yusuf, Kitab al-Kharaj (OpenITI / Internet Archive)

title: Ibn Sayyar al-Warraq's Kitab al-Tabikh (Abbasid Culinary Corpus)
description: Earliest extant Arabic cookbook from 4th/10th-century Baghdad, documenting Mesopotamian-Persianate culinary culture, crops, and dietary medicine.
